examples.ko: 시장에서 갓 튀긴 꽈배기를 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought and ate a freshly fried twisted doughnut at the market.
Twisted doughnuts taste even better coated with sugar.
I ordered a twisted doughnut and coffee as a snack.
I braided my hair into a twisted shape.

examples.ko: 이 집 꽈배기는 겉이 바삭하고 속이 쫄깃해요.
examples.en: This place's twisted doughnuts are crispy outside and chewy inside.

examples.ko: 꽈배기처럼 꼬인 줄을 푸느라 한참 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to untangle the rope twisted like a pretzel.

explain: 밀가루 반죽을 길게 꼬아서 튀긴 간식이에요. 무언가가 심하게 꼬인 모양을 말할 때 '꽈배기처럼'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a snack made of dough twisted into a long shape and fried. People also say '꽈배기처럼' when describing something badly twisted.

examples.en: In summer, jellyfish naengchae whets the appetite.
They served naengchae first as part of the feast.
You pour mustard sauce on this naengchae.
My mother made shrimp naengchae for us.

examples.ko: 냉채는 차게 먹는 요리라서 더운 날 좋아요.
examples.en: Naengchae is eaten cold, so it's nice on a hot day.
I ordered naengchae at a Chinese restaurant and it was refreshing.

explain: 여러 재료를 차게 해서 소스에 버무려 먹는 요리예요. 겨자나 식초가 들어간 새콤한 소스와 자주 먹고, 코스 요리에서는 처음에 나오는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a dish of several ingredients served cold and tossed in a sauce. It is often eaten with a tangy mustard or vinegar sauce and frequently comes first in a set course.

examples.en: I divide the cake equally into eight pieces.
The teacher divided the paper equally into three.
I will divide the field equally into four parts.
I shape the equally divided dough into rounds.

examples.ko: 수학 시간에 선분을 등분하는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In math class I learned how to divide a line segment equally.
I split my allowance into two equal parts and saved it.

explain: '몇 개로 등분하다'처럼 같은 크기로 나눌 때만 써요. 크기가 달라도 되는 '나누다'와 달리 조각이 모두 똑같아야 해요. 수학이나 요리 설명에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used only when dividing into equal sizes, as in 몇 개로 등분하다. Unlike 나누다, which allows unequal parts, 등분하다 needs every part to be the same size. It shows up often in math and cooking instructions.

p.s: 엄마가 케이크를 똑같이 여덟 개로 등분했어요.
p.o: 엄마가 케이크를 똑같이 여덟 개로 나눴어요.
p.n: 등분하다 says the parts are equal; 나누다 does not say that by itself.

examples.en: Fried tofu sushi is popular as a lunchbox item.
I ate udon with fried tofu in it.
I bought a bag of fried tofu pouches at the mart.
The fried tofu soaks up the broth, so it is delicious.
The child picks out only the fried tofu to eat.

examples.ko: 내일 점심에는 유부를 넣고 김밥을 말 거예요.
examples.en: For lunch tomorrow, I will roll gimbap with fried tofu in it.

explain: 한국에서는 '유부초밥', '유부우동'처럼 다른 음식 이름 안에 넣어 말하는 일이 많아요. 찌개나 부침에 넣는 '두부'와 쓰임이 달라서 둘을 바꿔 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: In Korea this word mostly shows up inside dish names like '유부초밥' and '유부우동'. It is used differently from plain '두부', which goes into stews and pan-fried dishes, so the two are not interchangeable.

examples.en: This restaurant is famous for its delicious à la carte dishes.
I'll order just one dish à la carte instead of the course.

examples.ko: 점심에는 일품요리를 싸게 파는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many places sell à la carte dishes cheaply at lunch.

examples.ko: 일품요리 메뉴에서 먹고 싶은 걸 골라 보세요.
examples.en: Pick what you want to eat from the à la carte menu.

examples.ko: 오늘은 갈비찜 같은 일품요리가 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: Today I want an à la carte dish like braised short ribs.
There are many customers, so à la carte orders are delayed.

explain: 메뉴판에서 '코스'나 '정식'과 나란히 나오는 말이에요. 여러 접시가 차례로 나오는 코스와 달리, 갈비찜이나 비빔밥처럼 한 접시로 식사가 되는 요리를 하나씩 골라 시킬 때 써요. '단품'은 세트가 아닌 메뉴 하나를 가리켜서 쓰임이 가깝지만 똑같지는 않아요.
explain_en: On a menu it appears alongside '코스' (course) and '정식' (set meal). Unlike a course with several plates in order, it is a dish like 갈비찜 or 비빔밥 that works as a meal on one plate and is ordered individually. '단품' (single item) is close in use, but it means one menu item that is not part of a set, so the two are not identical.

examples.en: I get starch from potatoes and use it in cooking.

examples.ko: 탕수육 소스는 전분 물을 넣어서 걸쭉하게 만들어요.
examples.en: You thicken sweet and sour sauce by adding starch water.
Rice contains a lot of starch.

examples.ko: 전분 가루가 없으면 밀가루로 대신해도 돼요?
examples.en: If I don't have starch powder, can I use flour instead?
Noodles made from potato starch are chewy.

examples.ko: 전분은 찬물에 잘 안 녹고 가라앉아요.
examples.en: Starch doesn't dissolve well in cold water and sinks.

explain: 요리에서는 '감자 전분', '옥수수 전분', '전분 가루'처럼 말하고, 같은 뜻으로 '녹말'도 써요. 영양이나 과학 이야기에서는 탄수화물의 한 종류로 나와요.
explain_en: In cooking it appears as '감자 전분', '옥수수 전분' and '전분 가루', and '녹말' is also used for the same thing. In nutrition and science talk it comes up as a kind of carbohydrate.

examples.ko: 시장에서 정어리를 싸게 사서 구워 먹었어요.
examples.en: I bought sardines cheaply at the market and grilled them.

examples.ko: 정어리는 값이 싸고 영양도 많은 생선이에요.
examples.en: Sardines are a cheap and nutritious fish.
Tonight's side dish is braised sardines.
Fresh sardines came into the supermarket.

examples.ko: 정어리랑 고등어 중에 뭐가 더 좋아요?
examples.en: Which do you like better, sardines or mackerel?
I've never cooked with sardines.

explain: 생선 이름이라 '정어리 구이', '정어리 조림'처럼 요리 이름과 같이 자주 말해요. 모양이 비슷해 보이는 '멸치'와는 다른 생선이에요.
explain_en: It is a fish name, often used in dish names like '정어리 구이' (grilled sardines) or '정어리 조림' (braised sardines). It may look similar to '멸치' (anchovy), but it is a different fish.

examples.en: I add a little salt when I cook.
No sugar was added to this snack.

examples.ko: 반죽에 우유를 첨가한 다음 잘 섞으세요.
examples.en: Add milk to the dough and then mix it well.
Fragrance was added to this shampoo.

examples.ko: 색소를 첨가하면 색이 더 진해질 거예요.
examples.en: If you add coloring, the color will get deeper.
This is bread made without preservatives.

explain: '넣다'는 어디에나 쓰지만 '첨가하다'는 음식, 약, 화학 제품에 무언가를 더할 때 주로 써요. 식품 성분표에는 '첨가물'이라는 말이 나와요. 글을 더할 때는 '덧붙이다'나 '추가하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 넣다 works almost anywhere, but 첨가하다 is used mainly for adding something to food, medicine or chemical products. On food labels you will see the word 첨가물 (additive). For adding words to a text, 덧붙이다 or 추가하다 sounds more natural.
